current_status.final_resting_site: Troy Sand Trap, West of Home Plate
current_status.cause_of_end: Right front wheel failure forced backward driving; rover broke through thin crust into hidden powdery iron sulfate sand, becoming permanently trapped; winter freeze ceased solar operations
current_status.historic_feat: Climbed Husband Hill (82 meters elevation rise); discovered 90% pure opaline silica proving ancient hydrothermal hot spring systems on Mars

traverse_summary.target_destination: Columbia Hills volcanic complex and hydrothermal deposits
key_milestones: Long march to base of Columbia Hills (Sol 156)
Summit of Husband Hill (Sol 582, 82m above plains)
Descent into Inner Basin & exploration of Home Plate (Sol 750)
Right front wheel jammed (Sol 779); dragged backward creating trench that exposed pure white silica (Sol 1150)
Last contact before martian winter (Sol 2210, March 2010)

waypoints.activity: Landing in basaltic rubble plain of Gusev Crater
Imaged 210m impact crater interior and heat shield debris
Reached ancient bedrock outcrops elevated above flood basalt plains
First mountain peak summited by a robotic rover on another world; panoramic 360-degree telemetry
Layered volcanic ash deposits and explosive phreatomagmatic bomb sag features examined
Dragged frozen wheel exposed brilliant white soil with >90% opaline silica, proving volcanic fumarole or hot springs
Rover crust breakthrough; trapped in powdery iron sulfate sand bank tilted at 12-degree adverse angle to sun; became permanent monument
waypoints.hazard_warning: FATAL WHEEL ENTRAPMENT - Powder sulfate sand trap
